name: Can drywall restoration permanently fix recurring settlement cracks?

mainEntity.name: Can drywall restoration permanently fix recurring settlement cracks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, fixing foundation or settling cracks in drywall requires stabilizing the seam rather than simply wiping spackle over the crack. In greater Denver and surrounding areas like Centennial and Parker, seasonal temperature swings and shifting soils frequently cause hairline cracks near door frames, window headers, and drywall joints. A surface-only spackle job will reopen within months. The proper approach involves widening the crack slightly to remove loose plaster, securing any loose drywall sheets to the underlying studs with fresh drywall screws, applying fiberglass mesh or paper tape embedded in setting compound, and finishing with lightweight mud to resist future micro-movements.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, if the seam is properly reinforced. Contractors secure loose panels to studs, embed durable tape in setting-type compound, and float the surface to resist movement.
